current_criteria.name: visual_grounding
current_criteria.description: The answer must accurately reflect what is visible in the image — describing objects, positions, colors, textures, and actions as they appear. It should not invent or misrepresent visual elements. Evaluated by direct comparison to the image content.

current_criteria.name: question_relevance
current_criteria.description: The answer must directly address the question asked, without drifting into irrelevant topics or tangential information. Evaluated by whether the answer’s core focus aligns with the question’s intent.

current_criteria.name: factual_consistency_with_the_image
current_criteria.description: The answer must not contain factual errors — such as misidentifying objects, their locations, or their states — that contradict the visual evidence. Evaluated by checking whether claims are visually verifiable.

current_criteria.name: avoidance_of_hallucinated_visual_details
current_criteria.description: The answer should not include details not present in the image — such as objects, actions, or attributes that are not visible or inferable with high confidence. Evaluated by flagging unsupported or invented visual claims.

current_criteria.name: completeness
current_criteria.description: The answer should cover all relevant aspects of the question without omitting key visual information. Evaluated by whether the response addresses all implied or explicit components of the question.

current_criteria.name: specificity
current_criteria.description: The answer should provide precise, detailed descriptions (e.g., exact locations, orientations, relative sizes) rather than vague or generalized statements. Evaluated by the level of detail and specificity in spatial or descriptive claims.

current_criteria.name: calibrated_uncertainty
current_criteria.description: The answer should use appropriate qualifiers (e.g., “possibly,” “likely,” “appears to be”) when describing uncertain or inferential content, and avoid overconfidence in unverifiable claims. Evaluated by whether the answer appropriately balances certainty and uncertainty.

current_criteria.name: clear_language
current_criteria.description: The answer should be grammatically correct, free of ambiguity, and use straightforward, natural language. Evaluated by readability, clarity, and absence of confusing or convoluted phrasing.

current_criteria.name: accuracy_of_visual_interpretation
current_criteria.description: The answer should correctly interpret visual cues — such as facial expressions, body posture, or object arrangement — without misattributing intent or emotion. Evaluated by whether visual inferences align with plausible real-world interpretations.

current_criteria.name: consistency_with_common_sense_or_domain_knowledge
current_criteria.description: The answer should not contradict basic knowledge about the world or the subject matter — e.g., biological plausibility, object behavior, or physical constraints. Evaluated by whether the answer aligns with known facts about the visual elements or context.

manager_prompt:
List and describe 10 criteria for how human annotators compare the quality of two answers to the same visual question.

The task is RLHF-V style preference comparison for visual question answering and image-text responses. The worker model will receive:
- the image,
- the source question,
- candidate answer A,
- candidate answer B.

Focus on human preference factors such as visual grounding, question relevance, factual consistency with the image, avoidance of hallucinated visual details, completeness, specificity, calibrated uncertainty, and clear language.
